settings.title: Start With Your Facility Type
settings.subheading: Every space has different demands. Tell us where your gym is going and we will tailor the equipment mix, durability level and layout guidance to how the room will actually be used.

settings.text: Reviewed by a Fitness Superstore gym specialist. Your details are used to prepare this quote.

settings.title: Around 500 sq. ft.
settings.text: A compact room where every piece has to earn its footprint. Expect a small cardio group, one multi-station strength unit or functional trainer, and a free weight corner with adjustable benches. Flooring and storage matter more here than machine count.

settings.title: Around 1,000 sq. ft.
settings.text: Enough room to separate cardio from strength. A wider cardio line, several selectorized machines covering the main movement patterns, a rack or half rack, and a dedicated free weight area with dumbbells across a usable weight range.

settings.title: Around 1,500 sq. ft.
settings.text: The point where a room starts to feel like a gym rather than an amenity. Room for a full cardio row, a broader selectorized circuit, plate-loaded pieces, a rack or rig, and an open functional zone that does not compete with the lifting area.

settings.title: 2,500 sq. ft. and above
settings.text: Planned in zones rather than as one room. Traffic patterns, sightlines and peak-hour flow drive the layout as much as the equipment list. Expect a full cardio bank, distinct selectorized and plate-loaded areas, multiple racks or a rig, and dedicated turf or functional space.

settings.title: Plan by Space and Traffic
settings.subheading: Room size is only part of the story. The right equipment mix also depends on who uses the space and how busy it gets. A quiet amenity room and a high-traffic commercial floor of the same size are planned very differently. The starting points below are conceptual planning guidance, not fixed packages.
settings.disclaimer: Conceptual equipment placement only. Final layouts require on-site verification and, where applicable, review by qualified professionals.

settings.title: Cardio
settings.text: Treadmills, ellipticals, bikes, rowers, steppers and climbers, sized to expected peak-hour use.

settings.title: Selectorized & Plate-Loaded Strength
settings.text: Pin-loaded circuits for guided use, plate-loaded machines for stronger, more experienced users, and multi-stack or jungle gym systems that let several people train strength at once in a shared footprint.

settings.title: Functional Trainers, Racks & Rigs
settings.text: Cable trainers, squat racks, half racks and rigs for barbell work and small group training.

settings.title: Free Weights & Benches
settings.text: Dumbbells, barbells, plates and adjustable or fixed benches with the racking to keep them in order.

settings.title: Flooring, Storage & Accessories
settings.text: Rubber flooring, turf, weight storage, mirrors and the accessories that keep a floor usable.

settings.title: Equipment Zones
settings.subheading: Most complete gyms are planned around a few core zones. Your specialist recommends specific options within each zone based on your space, users and budget. Tell us which zones you need and we will size them to your room.

settings.title: Share your room and project requirements
settings.text: Room size, ceiling height, facility type, budget and timing. A floor plan or photo helps but is not required.

settings.title: Review equipment mix and conceptual placement
settings.text: We put together an equipment list and a conceptual layout showing how the zones fit your room.

settings.title: Receive a tailored quote
settings.text: A quote built around your list, with condition options where new and remanufactured both make sense.

settings.title: Coordinate delivery, assembly or installation
settings.text: Where these services are available and approved for your project, we scope them alongside the equipment.

settings.title: New
settings.text: Current production models with the manufacturer's factory finish and console technology. Straightforward for facilities that want the newest equipment and a uniform look across the floor.

settings.title: Remanufactured
settings.text: Commercial-grade equipment restored for continued use, with condition and included work confirmed per item. A common route for facilities balancing equipment count and grade against the overall project budget.

settings.title: Mixed
settings.text: Many rooms end up here. New where console technology and finish matter most, remanufactured where a piece simply needs to work and hold up under traffic. We can flag which pieces are worth which approach in your room.

settings.title: New, Remanufactured or Mixed
settings.subheading: There is no single right answer. It depends on budget, expected traffic and how long the room needs to stay in service.
settings.disclaimer: Condition, coverage and availability are confirmed per item before you commit. No Best Value/Recommended badge. As Is is a separate, rare category and is never folded into Remanufactured.

settings.heading: Ready to Plan the Equipment for Your Room?

settings.text: Tell us what you want to see. A team member will confirm it's on the floor before your visit.

settings.title: How much does a commercial gym cost?
settings.text: There's no single price, because cost depends on your room size, the equipment zones you need, whether you choose new, remanufactured or mixed equipment, and any delivery or installation coordination. Rather than quote a generic figure, we prepare a tailored quote built around your facility, space and budget. Share your details and a specialist will put together numbers specific to your project.
Share your space, budget and timing and we will come back with an equipment mix, a conceptual layout and a quote.
